user_authority: 2026-10-06 message body: 'please continue by executing the engineering found in the document'. Jev advice status ESCALATE is advisory.
purpose: Test whether coupling the Q4 pre-projection novelty score s(q) into the Sagnac homodyne veto changes the dispatch decision, per the blueprint Delta_eff = Delta_Sagnac + lambda*(1 - s(q)).

design.s_q_source: novelty_gate.membership_score(psi_in, veto.axioms) -- the VETO'S OWN axiom bank, so one bank is used consistently
design.default_path: novelty_lambda=0.0 leaves delta_eff == delta_sagnac exactly; production behaviour is unchanged
design.dim_note: harness runs the small config (dim 4096); SagnacHomodyneVeto defaults to dim 65536. The measured configuration is 4096 and is disclosed in the receipt.

kill_conditions_frozen.K1_identity_at_lambda_0: lambda=0.0 reproduces the uncoupled verdict EXACTLY (allow equal elementwise) on every member of every family
kill_conditions_frozen.K2_heldout_vetoed: held-out corpus pass rate is 0.0 at lambda=0.5
kill_conditions_frozen.K3_inbank_preserved: in-bank pass rate stays 1.0 at lambda=0.5
kill_conditions_frozen.K4_attribution_control: replacing s(q) with a RANDOM score does NOT reproduce the held-out flip pattern. If a random score flips the same cases, the effect is not the novelty signal
kill_conditions_frozen.K5_determinism: two consecutive runs produce byte-identical receipts

non_tautology_disclosure: Criterion 1 (held-out vetoed) is NEARLY GUARANTEED by construction: held-out s ~ 0.21 makes the novelty penalty lambda*(1-s) ~ 0.40, which exceeds the 0.35 threshold REGARDLESS of delta_sagnac. Reporting that alone would repeat the tautology this session removed. The discriminating content is the NEAR-MISS BAND: F1/F2 score s = 0.72-0.99, so the penalty is only 0.005-0.14 and the flip depends on the actual delta_sagnac. The receipt therefore reports the per-family FLIP SPECTRUM, not just the extremes.
honest_scope: This tests whether the gate CHANGES A DISPATCH DECISION. It does not test whether HENRI is intelligent. The blueprint claims coupling 'elevates the net scored task rate'; no scored task is wired to the veto in this build, so the task-level claim is UNTESTED and is reported as such.
